subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider-level `models.providers.<provider>.enabled` config contract that disables routing while preserving the provider block?
rationale: The request is source-reproducible and fits provider ergonomics, but OpenClaw policy treats new config/default/provider-routing surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions rather than automatic bug repairs.

options.title: Approve bounded contract
options.body: Implement the flag across schema, models.json planning, configured catalogs, fallback resolution, and `models status`, with default-enabled compatibility and focused tests.

options.title: Decline the new config knob
options.body: Keep the current workaround of removing or editing provider blocks and avoid expanding persistent config surface.

options.title: Defer for provider-routing design
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers decide broader disabled-provider semantics for status, probes, auth, and fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded contract
recommendation.body: Implement the flag across schema, models.json planning, configured catalogs, fallback resolution, and `models status`, with default-enabled compatibility and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the affected model/config/status paths and already provided the prior detailed review of this issue.
